mainTopic: Which קרבן jobs a זר may do: the search for the source that הפשט וניתוח need no כהן, and the six כהנים who bring up the lamb.
overview: The גמרא asks which jobs in bringing a קרבן may be done by a זר (non-כהן). A ברייתא, explained by אביי, teaches that שחיטה is valid by a זר, and that from קבלה (receiving the blood) onward the work belongs only to כהנים. So when a פסוק mentions כהנים for a later job, that mention looks extra and can teach that some other job does NOT need a כהן. The גמרא tries three פסוקים as the source for letting a זר do הפשט וניתוח (skinning and cutting). The fire פסוק (״וְנָתְנוּ״) and ״וְעָרְכוּ״ are each shown to have their own lesson. In the end ״וְהִקְטִיר הַכֹּהֵן״ is the source. Along the way we learn from ״וְהִקְרִיב״ that carrying wood needs no כהן, while arranging the two logs does. ״וְעָרְכוּ בְּנֵי אַהֲרֹן הַכֹּהֲנִים״ teaches that six כהנים bring up the lamb. רבי אלעזר asks how a פסוק about a bull can teach this, and his answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The fire verse is needed for its own lesson
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges חזקיה: the פסוק about כהנים putting fire on the מזבח is needed to teach its own law, so it cannot be used to exclude הפשט וניתוח.
steps.simpleTranslation: But this verse is needed for itself!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks חזקיה's proof by saying the פסוק he used already has its own job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חזקיה read "וְנָתְנוּ בְּנֵי אַהֲרֹן" as saying 'only this job needs a כהן', which leaves out הפשט וניתוח. The objection is that the פסוק is simply telling us that putting fire on the מזבח needs a כהן. If the פסוק is needed for that plain lesson, there is no extra wording left to build an exclusion from.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed for (a different purpose)
For itself, for its own plain lesson
Skinning the animal
Cutting the animal into its parts

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying חזקיה's halacha is wrong. It only says that this particular פסוק looks too 'busy' to serve as his source.

phrases.english: But this verse is needed for its own sake!
phrases.notes: The verse is needed to teach that placing fire/wood on the altar requires a priest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks חזקיה's דרשה, which came on the previous amud.
steps.kashyaTarget: חזקיה's use of "וְנָתְנוּ בְּנֵי אַהֲרֹן" to exclude הפשט וניתוח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק needed for its own plain lesson has no extra room to teach an exclusion.

steps.title: אביי's ברייתא: slaughter by a non-priest is valid
steps.stepSummary: רב שימי בר אשי reports that he found אביי explaining חזקיה to his son with a ברייתא that starts: "וְשָׁחַט" teaches that שחיטה by a זר is כשרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שימי בר אשי said: I found אביי explaining it to his son. 'And he shall slaughter' teaches that slaughter by a non-priest is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer by bringing a ברייתא that אביי used. This step sets up a source that will show the fire פסוק is really extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא opens with a rule: since the פסוק says "וְשָׁחַט" without mentioning a כהן, anyone may do the שחיטה. The next lines of the ברייתא explain why this needed saying and where the כהן's role begins. That starting point is what will make the fire פסוק extra.

Explaining it to his son
Slaughtering the קרבן
A non-כהן
Valid

steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about שחיטה בזר, as explained by אביי

steps.title: Why we might have thought slaughter needs a priest
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks why we would ever think שחיטה needs a כהן. It answers: from "תִּשְׁמְרוּ אֶת כְּהוּנַּתְכֶם" we might have thought every part of the service needs a כהן, even שחיטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where would you come to think otherwise? From what is said: 'And you and your sons with you shall guard your priesthood.' From that I would understand that even slaughter needs a priest.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא pauses to explain why a פסוק was needed to allow a זר to do שחיטה. It shows the opposite idea we might have had.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The general פסוק "וְאַתָּה וּבָנֶיךָ אִתְּךָ תִּשְׁמְרוּ אֶת כְּהוּנַּתְכֶם" sounds like all עבודה belongs only to כהנים. So without a special teaching, we would have included שחיטה too. This sets up the next line, which will limit the כהן requirement.

keyTerms.meaning: From where would you come (to think this)?
From the fact that it says
Your priesthood
I would have understood

phrases.english: And from where would you come to think otherwise?
From the fact that it is said:
"And you and your sons with you
shall guard your priesthood,"
phrases.notes: Numbers 18:7

phrases.english: I would understand: even slaughter (requires a priest),

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the rule in step 2 needed a פסוק at all.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why would anyone think שחיטה requires a כהן?

steps.title: Priestly work starts from receiving the blood
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא proves from ויקרא 1:4–5 that the כהנים' exclusive work begins at קבלה (receiving the blood). שחיטה, done by the owner who did סמיכה, is valid by a זר.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse teaches: 'And he shall slaughter the young bull before ה׳, and the sons of Aaron, the priests, shall bring near the blood.' From receiving the blood and onward is the מצוה of priests. 'And he shall lean his hand… and slaughter' teaches that slaughter is valid by a non-priest.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives its answer. The כהנים are mentioned only starting with the blood, so their exclusive job runs from קבלה onward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two points come from the פסוקים. First, the כהנים are named only when the blood is brought near, which begins with קבלה, so from there on is מצות כהונה. Second, the same person who does סמיכה, the owner, is the one who does "וְשָׁחַט". That shows שחיטה is כשרה בזר.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק teaches
Receiving the blood in a כלי
A job only for כהנים
And he shall lean (his hands on the קרבן)

steps.whyThisMatters: The rule "מקבלה ואילך מצות כהונה" is the key that makes the fire פסוק look extra in the next step.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The כהנים' exclusive work starts at קבלה, and שחיטה is valid by a זר.

steps.title: So the fire verse is extra and excludes skinning and cutting
steps.stepSummary: אביי reasons that since everything from קבלה onward already needs a כהן, "וְנָתְנוּ בְּנֵי אַהֲרֹן" about the fire is extra. It is used to exclude הפשט וניתוח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, since from receiving the blood onward is the מצוה of priests, why do I need 'and the sons of Aaron shall put'? To exclude skinning and cutting up.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the actual answer to the קשיא in step 1. The fire פסוק is not needed for its own lesson, so it teaches an exclusion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Putting fire on the מזבח comes after קבלה, so we would already know it needs a כהן from the ברייתא. The פסוק saying "בני אהרן" again is therefore extra. It shows that only this kind of job needs a כהן, while הפשט וניתוח may be done by a זר.

keyTerms.meaning: Now, since (we already know)
Why do I need it?
To exclude
And they shall put (the fire)

steps.whatToRemember: Defense of חזקיה: since "מקבלה ואילך מצות כהונה", the fire פסוק is extra and comes to exclude הפשט וניתוח.

phrases.english: Now, since from receiving the blood onward is the מצוה of the priesthood,
why do I need "and the sons of Aaron shall put"?
phrases.notes: Leviticus 1:7, putting fire on the altar.

phrases.english: To exclude skinning and cutting up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא's rule from step 4 to answer the קשיא of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the פסוק is extra (ייתור), so it is free for a דרשה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The fire פסוק is needed just to teach that fire placement needs a כהן.
steps.terutzMaskana: That is already known from "מקבלה ואילך", so the פסוק excludes הפשט וניתוח.

steps.title: The fire verse may still be needed for jobs that do not block atonement
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: the fire פסוק is still needed. Since putting wood or fire is not a job that holds back כפרה, we might have thought it needs no כהן, so the פסוק teaches that it does.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is still needed! You might have said: since it is not a service that holds back atonement, it does not need a priest. So the verse teaches us that it does need a priest.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges אביי's answer by showing a real reason the fire פסוק is needed for itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule "מקבלה ואילך" might only cover jobs tied to the blood, which brings כפרה. Placing the fire is not something כפרה depends on, so without the פסוק we might have let a זר do it. Once the פסוק has this job, it is not extra, and חזקיה's exclusion of הפשט וניתוח is in doubt again.

keyTerms.meaning: But it is still needed
You might have thought
A service that holds back atonement
It teaches us

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read the end "קא משמע לן דבעיא כהונה" as the גמרא concluding the issue. It is part of the attack: it shows the פסוק has its own lesson, which undoes the answer of step 5.

phrases.english: But it is still needed:
it might have entered your mind to say
since it is not a service
that holds back atonement —
it should not need priesthood,
so it teaches us that it does need priesthood!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 5 by giving the fire פסוק its own lesson.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that "וְנָתְנוּ בְּנֵי אַהֲרֹן" is extra
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: "מקבלה ואילך" might cover only jobs that bring כפרה. The fire job is not one of them, so the פסוק is needed to require a כהן for it and is not extra.

steps.title: A new source: "And they shall lay out" excludes flaying and cutting
steps.stepSummary: Since the fire פסוק is needed for its own lesson, the גמרא uses "וְעָרְכוּ בְּנֵי אַהֲרֹן הַכֹּהֲנִים" as the extra פסוק that excludes הפשט וניתוח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, learn it from here: "And Aaron's sons, the priests, shall lay out the pieces, the head and the fat." Everything from קבלה onward already needs a כהן, so why do I need "and they shall lay out"? It comes to exclude flaying and cutting.
steps.whatsHappening: The old source was knocked out, so the גמרא brings a new extra פסוק to teach that הפשט וניתוח do not need a כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The logic is the same one אביי used before. Anything after קבלה already needs a כהן, so a פסוק that says 'כהנים' about a later job is extra. An extra mention of כהנים is read as teaching that a different, similar job does NOT need a כהן. Only the פסוק has changed: it is now the one about laying out the pieces instead of the one about fire.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, from here (a new source replacing a rejected one)
And they shall lay out / arrange (the pieces on the מזבח)
The cut-up pieces of the animal
Since / after all (introduces an obvious premise)
Skinning the animal and cutting it into pieces

phrases.english: Rather, from here:
phrases.notes: The fire פסוק was shown to be needed, so a new source is brought.

phrases.english: "And Aaron's sons, the priests, shall lay out

steps.terutzHavaAmina: The fire פסוק teaches that הפשט וניתוח are excluded.
steps.terutzMaskana: The fire פסוק is needed for wood and fire, so "וְעָרְכוּ" is the extra פסוק that excludes הפשט וניתוח.

steps.title: Maybe the פסוק excludes arranging the two logs instead
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: perhaps "וְעָרְכוּ" comes to exclude סידור שני גזירי עצים, not הפשט וניתוח.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say it comes to exclude the arranging of the two logs of wood!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how we know which job the extra פסוק is excluding. Maybe it is arranging the two logs on the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An extra פסוק can exclude something, but the פסוק does not name what. The challenger suggests a different candidate: placing the two logs of wood. If that is right, we would lose our source for הפשט וניתוח.

keyTerms.meaning: But say (introduces an alternative reading)
Arranging the two logs of wood placed on the מזבח

phrases.english: But say it comes to exclude
the arranging of the two logs of wood!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵימָא לְמַעוֹטֵי סִידּוּר שְׁנֵי גְּזִירֵי עֵצִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions which job the new source from Step 7 is excluding.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that "וְעָרְכוּ" excludes הפשט וניתוח.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An exclusion does not name its target. סידור עצים is an equally possible candidate, so the proof for הפשט וניתוח is not certain.

steps.title: It makes more sense to exclude a job on the animal itself
steps.stepSummary: The pieces are part of the animal, so the פסוק more likely excludes another job done to the animal, which is הפשט וניתוח.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is more reasonable that it excludes a service similar to itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a פסוק usually excludes something similar to what it is talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "וְעָרְכוּ" is about the pieces of the animal. Skinning and cutting are also done to the animal's body, while the wood is not part of the animal at all. So the closer match is הפשט וניתוח.

keyTerms.meaning: It is more logical / reasonable
A service done on the sacrifice (the animal)
Similar to it

phrases.english: It is more reasonable that it excludes a service on the animal, which is similar to it.
phrases.notes: Laying out pieces and skinning/cutting both involve the animal's body.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 8 with a similarity argument.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Logical similarity (exclude what is most alike)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק might exclude the wood.
steps.terutzMaskana: It excludes the job that, like itself, is done on the animal: הפשט וניתוח.

steps.title: On the contrary, arranging wood is more similar
steps.stepSummary: The challenger flips the argument: "וְעָרְכוּ" means arranging, so arranging the wood is the closer match.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary, it excludes arranging, which is similar to it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back with an opposite similarity. The פסוק is about arranging, and placing logs is also arranging.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Similarity can be measured two ways. One way looks at the object, the animal. The other looks at the action, arranging things on the מזבח. By the action, סידור עצים looks more like "וְעָרְכוּ" than skinning does, so logic alone cannot decide.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary
Arranging / placing in order

phrases.english: On the contrary, it excludes arranging, which is similar to it!
phrases.notes: Both are acts of placing something on the מזבח.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reverses the similarity argument of Step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the animal-related job is the closer match.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Similarity by action (arranging) is just as strong as similarity by object (the animal), so the logic of Step 9 can point the other way.

steps.title: Another פסוק proves that arranging the logs needs a כהן
steps.stepSummary: From "וְהִקְרִיב הַכֹּהֵן אֶת הַכֹּל" we learn that only carrying limbs needs כהונה and carrying wood does not. This implies that arranging the two logs does need a כהן, so "וְעָרְכוּ" cannot be excluding it.
steps.simpleTranslation: That cannot enter your mind, because the Master said: "And the priest shall bring all of it to the altar" refers to carrying the limbs to the ramp. Carrying the limbs to the ramp is what needs priesthood, and carrying wood does not need priesthood. This implies that arranging the two logs does need priesthood!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the challenge by bringing a separate source. That source already decides the law for the wood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "וְהִקְרִיב הַכֹּהֵן" is also an extra mention of a כהן after קבלה, and it teaches that carrying wood does not need a כהן. Since the Torah excluded only carrying the wood, the actual arranging of the logs stays in the כהן's category. So "וְעָרְכוּ" cannot be excluding the wood, and it must be excluding הפשט וניתוח.

keyTerms.meaning: It cannot enter your mind (strong rejection)
Carrying the limbs to the ramp of the מזבח
The ramp leading up to the מזבח
Carrying the wood to the מזבח

steps.whatToRemember: Skinning and cutting the animal (הפשט וניתוח) and carrying the wood do NOT need a כהן. Carrying the limbs to the ramp and arranging the two logs on the מזבח DO need a כהן.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up carrying the wood (הולכת עצים), which a זר may do, with arranging the logs on the מזבח (סידור), which needs a כהן. They are two different jobs with opposite rules.
steps.whyThisMatters: This settles the challenge of Step 10. Carrying wood is excluded by "וְהִקְרִיב", and by implication arranging the two logs still needs a כהן, so "וְעָרְכוּ" must be excluding הפשט וניתוח. Step 12 will challenge even that, and Step 13 replaces "וְעָרְכוּ" with "וְהִקְטִיר".

phrases.english: It cannot enter your mind,
for the Master said:
"And the priest shall bring all of it to the altar,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 1:13

phrases.english: this is carrying the limbs to the ramp.
Carrying the limbs to the ramp
is what needs priesthood,
carrying wood does not need priesthood.
phrases.notes: This is the exclusion that the extra mention of a כהן teaches.

phrases.english: This implies that arranging the two logs of wood
does need priesthood!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defeats the challenge in Step 10 with an outside source, which confirms the reading in Step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Outside source already decides the case
steps.terutzMaskana: Arranging the logs needs a כהן (only carrying wood is excluded), so "וְעָרְכוּ" excludes הפשט וניתוח.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: הפשט וניתוח and carrying wood may be done by a זר. Arranging the two logs requires a כהן.

steps.title: The verse about arranging has its own lesson
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא repeats its earlier claim that ״וְעָרְכוּ״ excludes הפשט וניתוח, and then attacks it: maybe this verse is needed for its own lesson.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need ״וְעָרְכוּ״? To exclude skinning and cutting up. But say that this verse too is needed for its own lesson!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings back its earlier answer, that ״וְעָרְכוּ״ teaches that skinning and cutting do not need a כהן. Now it challenges that answer: this verse may be busy teaching something else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An 'extra' verse can only teach an exclusion if it has nothing else to teach. The fire verse was already rejected for this reason (Step 6). Now the same problem hits ״וְעָרְכוּ״, because it also has its own lesson, which the גמרא will show in Step 15.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need it? This asks what a verse is there to teach.
To exclude, meaning to take something out of a rule
Skinning the animal and cutting it into pieces
For itself, meaning needed to teach its own lesson

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a brand-new question. The גמרא is quoting its own earlier answer (from Step 7) only so that it can knock it down.

phrases.english: Why do I need "and they shall arrange"?
phrases.notes: Repeats the earlier question so it can be challenged

phrases.english: To exclude skinning and cutting up.
phrases.notes: The earlier answer from Step 7

phrases.english: But say that this too is needed for its own lesson!
phrases.notes: Same attack that was used against the fire verse

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After Step 11 defended ״וְעָרְכוּ״ against the logs reading, the גמרא now raises a new problem with using it at all.
steps.kashyaTarget: The derivation in Step 7 that ״וְעָרְכוּ״ excludes הפשט וניתוח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A verse that is needed for its own lesson is not free to teach an exclusion. ״וְעָרְכוּ״ has its own lesson, so it cannot be the source.

steps.title: The burning verse is the real source
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא switches to a new verse, ״וְהִקְטִיר הַכֹּהֵן אֶת הַכֹּל״, as the source that excludes הפשט וניתוח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: what does ״וְהִקְטִיר הַכֹּהֵן אֶת הַכֹּל״ come to teach? To exclude skinning and cutting up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops ״וְעָרְכוּ״ and picks a new verse about burning the animal. It says this verse is the one that teaches that skinning and cutting do not need a כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Burning on the מזבח comes after the blood is collected (קבלה), and we already know that every job from קבלה onward needs a כהן. So the word הַכֹּהֵן in this verse is not needed for burning itself, and it is free to teach something else. What it teaches is that other jobs done to the animal, skinning and cutting, do not need a כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, which signals that an earlier idea is dropped and a new one is offered
And he shall burn (on the מִזְבֵּחַ)
For what does it come? What is this verse here to teach?

steps.whatToRemember: The final source that a non-כהן may skin and cut up the קרבן is ״וְהִקְטִיר הַכֹּהֵן אֶת הַכֹּל״.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 12 by replacing ״וְעָרְכוּ״ with a verse that has no lesson of its own.

steps.terutzMaskana: ״וְהִקְטִיר הַכֹּהֵן״ is the extra verse, because burning already needs a כהן as a job that comes after קבלה.

steps.title: Summing up what the other verses teach
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reviews the lessons: ״וְהִקְרִיב״ teaches that carrying limbs needs a כהן but carrying wood does not, which shows that arranging the two logs does need a כהן. ״וְנָתְנוּ״ teaches its own lesson.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And the priest shall bring all of it to the altar" refers to carrying the limbs to the ramp. Carrying limbs to the ramp needs a כהן; carrying wood does not need a כהן. This implies that arranging the two logs does need a כהן. "And they shall put" (the fire) is needed for its own lesson.
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the sources have been sorted out, the גמרא wraps up by listing what each of the other verses teaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״וְהִקְרִיב״ shows that carrying limbs to the כבש needs a כהן, and it excludes carrying wood. Because only carrying the wood is left out, arranging the two logs stays a job for a כהן. ״וְנָתְנוּ״ (putting the fire on the מזבח) teaches its own lesson, that this job must be done by כהנים, so it does not exclude anything.

steps.whatToRemember: Carrying limbs needs a כהן, carrying wood does not, and arranging the two logs does. Skinning and cutting do not need a כהן (learned from ״וְהִקְטִיר״).

steps.title: Each plural word adds two priests, making six
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows the own lesson of ״וְעָרְכוּ בְּנֵי אַהֲרֹן הַכֹּהֲנִים״: three plural words, each meaning two, teach that the lamb is brought up by six כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And they shall arrange" means two. "The sons of Aaron" means two more. "The priests" means two more. We learn that the lamb needs six priests.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains what ״וְעָרְכוּ״ teaches on its own. This is the lesson that made it unusable as an exclusion back in Step 12.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A plural word means at least two. The verse has three plural words, ״וְעָרְכוּ״, ״בְּנֵי אַהֲרֹן״ and ״הַכֹּהֲנִים״, so they add up to six. This matches the earlier משנה, where the limbs of the lamb were carried by six כהנים.

keyTerms.meaning: Two, the smallest number a plural word can mean
A lamb (here, the lamb of the קָרְבַּן תָּמִיד)
Needs six (כֹּהֲנִים)
We have learned

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the challenge in Step 12 was real: ״וְעָרְכוּ״ truly has its own lesson. It also gives a Torah source for the number of כהנים in the משנה.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not count the words as one priest each. Every plural word counts as two, so three words make six, not three.

phrases.notes: The verb is plural, so that means two.

phrases.english: "The sons of Aaron": two.
phrases.notes: "Sons" is plural, so that means two.

phrases.english: "The priests": two.
phrases.notes: "Priests" is plural, so that means two.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the 'own lesson' (לגופיה) of ״וְעָרְכוּ״ that was raised in Step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The lamb's limbs must be brought up by six כהנים, learned from the three plural words in ״וְעָרְכוּ בְּנֵי אַהֲרֹן הַכֹּהֲנִים״.

steps.title: The verse is about a bull, and a bull needs twenty-four
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא reports that רבי אלעזר found the source for 'six כהנים' difficult. The verse ״וְעָרְכוּ בְּנֵי אַהֲרֹן הַכֹּהֲנִים״ is written about a בן בקר (young bull), and a bull is brought by twenty-four כהנים, not six.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב המנונא said: This was difficult for רבי אלעזר. This verse is written about a young bull, and a young bull needs twenty-four כהנים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a problem with the source it just gave for six כהנים. The verse it used is about a bull, not a lamb.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 15 the גמרא counted three plural words to reach six כהנים for the lamb of the תמיד. But that verse sits in the section about an עולה from cattle (בן בקר). We already know a bull is brought by twenty-four כהנים. So how can a bull verse be the source for a lamb, and give a number that doesn't even match bulls?

keyTerms.meaning: It was difficult for him; he had a question
A young bull (cattle offering)
It is written
Requires / needs

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי אלעזר is saying the lamb needs twenty-four. He accepts that a lamb needs six. His only problem is that the verse used as the source is about a bull.

steps.kashyaTarget: The use of ״וְעָרְכוּ בְּנֵי אַהֲרֹן הַכֹּהֲנִים״ as the source that a lamb is brought by six כהנים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The verse is about a bull, and a bull is brought by twenty-four כהנים. So the verse cannot directly teach a rule of six for a lamb.

steps.title: The extra words 'wood, fire, altar' hint to a different offering
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר resolves his own question. The phrase ״עַל הָעֵצִים אֲשֶׁר עַל הָאֵשׁ אֲשֶׁר עַל הַמִּזְבֵּחַ״ seems to add nothing about the bull. So it is read as a hint: which offering is the one about which wood, fire, and altar are mentioned? The answer comes on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it was resolved for him: The verse says "On the wood that is on the fire upon the altar." Which is the item about which wood, fire, and altar are stated?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר starts answering his own question. He asks which offering is described with wood, fire, and altar. This line sets up the answer, and the גמרא names that offering on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'on the wood that is on the fire upon the altar' teach nothing new about the bull. So they are taken as a pointer to another offering, one the Torah connects with wood, fire, and altar. That offering (the תמיד, a lamb) is the one the six-כהנים rule really applies to. This takes the verse's lesson away from the bull.

steps.confusionAlert: The answer is not finished on this amud. The question 'which item has wood, fire, and altar?' is answered on the next amud, where the גמרא names the תמיד.
